paragraphs.title: The Lord Is the Levites’ Inheritance

easy.question: Which tribe will have no share and inheritance with Israel?
answers: Judah
Levi
Benjamin
easy.explanation: The passage says that the tribe of Levi will have no share or inheritance with the rest of Israel.

easy.question: What will the priests and Levites eat?
answers: The offerings of the Lord made by fire and his inheritance
All the produce of the land
The spoils of war
easy.explanation: The passage says that they will eat the Lord’s offerings and his inheritance.

easy.question: Who is the inheritance of the tribe of Levi?
answers: Moses
The people of Israel
The Lord
easy.explanation: The passage states explicitly, “The Lord is his inheritance.”

medium.question: In the phrase “they shall have no inheritance among their brethren,” what does “inheritance” mean?
answers: A share or estate, especially in the land
A sacrifice eaten at the sanctuary
A leadership position
medium.explanation: In this context, an inheritance is a share or estate within the land of Israel.

medium.question: What is the connection between Levi having no inheritance and what he receives?
answers: He receives Israel’s kingdom
The Lord is his inheritance, and he eats the Lord’s offerings
He receives a double inheritance
medium.explanation: Although Levi has no ordinary land inheritance, the Lord and his offerings are presented as Levi’s source of inheritance.

medium.question: What idea is repeated in both verses?
answers: The tribe of Levi has no ordinary inheritance among Israel’s tribes
All the tribes eat only sacrifices
The tribe of Levi receives most of the land
medium.explanation: Both verses emphasize that Levi has no share or inheritance among the other Israelites.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “all the tribe of Levi”?
answers: Only priests from Aaron’s family are included
Only Levites serving at the sanctuary are included
The instruction applies to the entire tribe of Levi
challenge.explanation: The phrase broadens the reference to the whole tribe, not merely to certain people within it.

challenge.question: Why should we not conclude that the tribe of Levi has no means of support?
answers: Because it receives all the land of Israel
Because it eats the Lord’s offerings and his inheritance
Because it collects taxes from Judah alone
challenge.explanation: Although Levi has no land inheritance, the passage identifies another source of support: the Lord’s offerings and inheritance.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between Levi and the other tribes in these verses?
answers: The other tribes have land inheritances, while the Lord is Levi’s inheritance
The other tribes have no food, while Levi has food
The other tribes have a sanctuary, while Levi has none
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts Israel’s land inheritance with the Lord as the special inheritance of Levi.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “all the tribe of Levi”?
answers: Only priests from Aaron’s family are included
Only Levites serving at the sanctuary are included
The instruction applies to the entire tribe of Levi
questions.explanation: The phrase broadens the reference to the whole tribe, not merely to certain people within it.

questions.question: Why should we not conclude that the tribe of Levi has no means of support?
answers: Because it receives all the land of Israel
Because it eats the Lord’s offerings and his inheritance
Because it collects taxes from Judah alone
questions.explanation: Although Levi has no land inheritance, the passage identifies another source of support: the Lord’s offerings and inheritance.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between Levi and the other tribes in these verses?
answers: The other tribes have land inheritances, while the Lord is Levi’s inheritance
The other tribes have no food, while Levi has food
The other tribes have a sanctuary, while Levi has none
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts Israel’s land inheritance with the Lord as the special inheritance of Levi.

paragraphs.title: The Priests’ Portions from Sacrifices and Produce

easy.question: Which parts of an ox or sheep are given to the priest?
answers: The shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach
The head, feet, and hide
The blood, fat, and horns
easy.explanation: The passage says that the priest receives the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach from the ox or sheep.

easy.question: Which gifts from the produce are given to the priest?
answers: All the grain
The firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil, and the first fleece of the sheep
Only the fruit of trees
easy.explanation: The passage commands the people to give the priest the firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil, and the first fleece of the sheep.

easy.question: Why did the Lord choose the priests?
answers: To manage trade
To guard the flocks
To stand and minister in the Lord’s name continually
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord chose them to minister in his name, they and their sons, forever.

medium.question: What order of events is described regarding an ox or sheep offered as a sacrifice?
answers: The animal is sacrificed, and then certain parts are given to the priest
The priest raises the animal, and then the people eat it
The entire animal is given to the priest before it is sacrificed
medium.explanation: The passage first refers to sacrificing an ox or sheep and then commands that certain portions be given to the priest.

medium.question: In the phrase “the firstfruit of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil,” what does “wine” refer to?
answers: Your grain
Your wine
Your fleece
medium.explanation: The phrase lists wine alongside grain and oil as agricultural produce.

medium.question: How are the gifts to the priests connected to their role?
answers: The gifts are only for people who raise cattle
The gifts replace the priests’ work
The gifts are given to priests chosen to minister in the Lord’s name
medium.explanation: The passage presents the gifts and then explains that the Lord chose the priests for his service.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice”?
answers: The gifts are especially connected with those who bring a sacrifice
Only priests are allowed to sacrifice
The gifts are taken from everyone regardless of what they do
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the gifts come from the people, particularly from those who offer sacrifices.

challenge.question: What does “he and his sons forever” teach about the priests’ service?
answers: Only one priest serves in each period
The service continues through the priests’ sons
The service ends after one sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The phrase includes both the priest and his sons and emphasizes the continuation of the priestly service.

challenge.question: What is the significance of the repeated idea of the “first” portion in verse 4?
answers: The priest must receive all the produce
Only defective produce may be given to the priest
The first and best portion of the produce is dedicated to the priest
challenge.explanation: The first portion refers to the beginning or best part of the grain, wine, oil, and fleece, not all the produce.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice”?
answers: The gifts are especially connected with those who bring a sacrifice
Only priests are allowed to sacrifice
The gifts are taken from everyone regardless of what they do
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the gifts come from the people, particularly from those who offer sacrifices.

questions.question: What does “he and his sons forever” teach about the priests’ service?
answers: Only one priest serves in each period
The service continues through the priests’ sons
The service ends after one sacrifice
questions.explanation: The phrase includes both the priest and his sons and emphasizes the continuation of the priestly service.

questions.question: What is the significance of the repeated idea of the “first” portion in verse 4?
answers: The priest must receive all the produce
Only defective produce may be given to the priest
The first and best portion of the produce is dedicated to the priest
questions.explanation: The first portion refers to the beginning or best part of the grain, wine, oil, and fleece, not all the produce.

paragraphs.title: The Levite Who Comes to Serve at the Sanctuary

easy.question: Who may come and serve at the place the Lord chooses?
answers: A Levite
The king
A prophet
easy.explanation: The passage concerns a Levite who comes from his residence to the place the Lord chooses.

easy.question: Where does the Levite live before coming to the place the Lord chooses?
answers: Only in Jerusalem
In one of the cities of Israel
In the king’s palace
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Levite comes from one of the gates of Israel, meaning that he lives in one of Israel’s cities.

easy.question: With whom will the Levite serve at the place the Lord chooses?
answers: With the people of Judah
With the priests only
With his fellow Levites
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Levite will serve like all his fellow Levites.

medium.question: What happens when the Levite greatly desires to come to the place the Lord chooses?
answers: He may come and serve there
He must remain in his city
He becomes a priest
medium.explanation: When the Levite comes with all the desire of his heart to the chosen place, he may serve there like the other Levites.

medium.question: In the phrase “where he sojourned,” what does “sojourned” mean?
answers: Fought there
Lived there
Sold things there
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the place where the Levite resides before coming to the chosen place.

medium.question: What order of events is described in the passage?
answers: The Levite eats, then comes, and finally serves
The Levite serves in his city, is sold, and finally comes
The Levite comes, serves with his fellow Levites, and receives an equal portion
medium.explanation: First the Levite comes to the chosen place, then he serves with his fellow Levites, and he receives an equal portion.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the Levite may come “from any of thy gates out of all Israel”?
answers: Service is not limited to Levites who live near the chosen place
Only a Levite from Jerusalem may serve
Anyone from Israel can become a Levite
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that a Levite from anywhere in the land may come and serve at the place the Lord chooses.

challenge.question: What does “like portions” mean in the context of the Levites?
answers: Each Levite receives a completely different role
The visiting Levite receives an equal share with his fellow Levites
The Levite must give his entire share to others
challenge.explanation: “Like portions” expresses equality: the Levite who comes from elsewhere eats a portion like his fellow Levites.

challenge.question: What exception follows the command that the Levite receive an equal portion?
answers: He may not serve with his fellow Levites
He receives only half a portion
This does not include what comes from the sale of his family inheritance
challenge.explanation: The passage makes an exception for matters connected with the sale of his ancestral inheritance.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the Levite may come “from any of thy gates out of all Israel”?
answers: Service is not limited to Levites who live near the chosen place
Only a Levite from Jerusalem may serve
Anyone from Israel can become a Levite
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that a Levite from anywhere in the land may come and serve at the place the Lord chooses.

questions.question: What does “like portions” mean in the context of the Levites?
answers: Each Levite receives a completely different role
The visiting Levite receives an equal share with his fellow Levites
The Levite must give his entire share to others
questions.explanation: “Like portions” expresses equality: the Levite who comes from elsewhere eats a portion like his fellow Levites.

questions.question: What exception follows the command that the Levite receive an equal portion?
answers: He may not serve with his fellow Levites
He receives only half a portion
This does not include what comes from the sale of his family inheritance
questions.explanation: The passage makes an exception for matters connected with the sale of his ancestral inheritance.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of the Nations’ Practices

easy.question: What does the passage command the Israelites when they enter the land?
answers: Not to learn to practice the abominations of the nations
To learn the customs of the nations
To leave the land
easy.explanation: The passage commands Israel not to learn the detestable practices of the nations in the land.

easy.question: Which of the following is not included in the list of forbidden practices?
answers: Divination
Honoring parents
Consulting the dead
easy.explanation: The passage mentions divination and consulting the dead, but it does not mention honoring parents.

easy.question: What does the Lord do to the nations because of their abominations?
answers: He protects them
He teaches them
He drives them out before Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that because of these abominations, the Lord drives the nations out before Israel.

medium.question: Why are Israelites forbidden to practice the things mentioned in these verses?
answers: Because they are difficult to understand
Because they are an abomination to the Lord
Because they belong only to priests
medium.explanation: The passage explains that everyone who does these things is an abomination to the Lord.

medium.question: What is the main sequence of ideas in these verses?
answers: Israel enters the land, is commanded not to imitate the nations, and is told why
The nations return home, and Israel then learns their practices
Israel asks for a sign, and the Lord gives them the land
medium.explanation: The passage first describes Israel entering the land, then forbids imitating the nations, and finally explains the reason.

medium.question: In the phrase “all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord,” what does “abomination” mean?
answers: A special commandment
A hidden thing
A detestable and hated thing
medium.explanation: An abomination is something detestable and rejected; the context shows that the Lord hates and forbids these practices.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the many forms of divination and seeking hidden knowledge listed in the passage?
answers: The prohibition is broad and includes various forbidden ways of seeking knowledge or power
Some of these practices are allowed if they work
The prohibition applies only to people who are not Israelites
challenge.explanation: The many examples show that the prohibition is not limited to one practice but includes different forms of magic, divination, and consulting the dead.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “There shall not be found among you” mean in this context?
answers: Only the king may not practice these things
Such practices must not be found among the people of Israel
These practices are allowed only outside the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase addresses the whole nation and emphasizes that such practices must not exist among Israelites.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the nations’ abominations and Israel’s possessing the land?
answers: The nations left the land entirely by their own choice
Israel received the land because it learned the nations’ practices
The Lord drives out the nations because of their detestable practices
challenge.explanation: The passage directly connects the nations’ abominations with the Lord driving them out before Israel.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the many forms of divination and seeking hidden knowledge listed in the passage?
answers: The prohibition is broad and includes various forbidden ways of seeking knowledge or power
Some of these practices are allowed if they work
The prohibition applies only to people who are not Israelites
questions.explanation: The many examples show that the prohibition is not limited to one practice but includes different forms of magic, divination, and consulting the dead.

questions.question: What does the phrase “There shall not be found among you” mean in this context?
answers: Only the king may not practice these things
Such practices must not be found among the people of Israel
These practices are allowed only outside the land
questions.explanation: The phrase addresses the whole nation and emphasizes that such practices must not exist among Israelites.

questions.question: What is the connection between the nations’ abominations and Israel’s possessing the land?
answers: The nations left the land entirely by their own choice
Israel received the land because it learned the nations’ practices
The Lord drives out the nations because of their detestable practices
questions.explanation: The passage directly connects the nations’ abominations with the Lord driving them out before Israel.

paragraphs.title: Being Wholehearted with the Lord and Separate from the Nations

easy.question: How does the Lord command Israel to be?
answers: Wholehearted with the Lord their God
Like the nations
Followers of diviners
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God.”

easy.question: Whom do the nations described in the passage listen to?
answers: The prophets of Israel
Observers of times and diviners
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: The passage says that the nations listen to observers of times and diviners.

easy.question: What are the Israelites told in relation to the ways of the nations?
answers: They must do exactly as the nations do
They must learn from them
They must not practice in that way
easy.explanation: The passage contrasts Israel with the nations and says that Israel must not act as they do.

medium.question: Why does the Torah emphasize that Israel must not be like the nations?
answers: Because the nations worshiped only the Lord
Because the nations turned to diviners and observers of times
Because the nations did not want the land
medium.explanation: The passage connects the command to be wholehearted with the nations’ reliance on diviners and observers of times.

medium.question: What sequence is described in the passage?
answers: Israel consults diviners and then possesses the nations
The nations leave the land and Israel listens to them
Israel possesses the nations but does not adopt their ways
medium.explanation: The passage refers to the nations Israel will possess and immediately emphasizes that Israel must not act like them.

medium.question: In the phrase “Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God,” what does “perfect” mean?
answers: Wholehearted and upright, trusting the Lord instead of using magic
Weak and inexperienced
Sad and worried
medium.explanation: In context, being perfect means being wholehearted and upright with the Lord rather than seeking guidance through forbidden practices.

challenge.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the contrast between the nations and Israel?
answers: Israel has another way to receive guidance: faithfulness to the Lord
Israel should learn the secrets of diviners
The nations believe in nothing
challenge.explanation: The passage presents Israel’s faithfulness to the Lord as the opposite of the nations’ reliance on diviners.

challenge.question: What does “which thou shalt possess” imply in the context of this command?
answers: Israel must adopt the customs of the people in the land
Even after possessing the land, Israel must not adopt its inhabitants’ practices
Israel will never enter the land
challenge.explanation: The passage warns that even when Israel possesses the land, it must remain separate from the practices of its former inhabitants.

challenge.question: What important contrast is expressed by “but as for thee”?
answers: It compares Israel with the nations
It says that the nations do not exist
It emphasizes a clear difference between Israel and the nations
challenge.explanation: The phrase marks a strong contrast: Israel is not to follow the ways of the nations.

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the contrast between the nations and Israel?
answers: Israel has another way to receive guidance: faithfulness to the Lord
Israel should learn the secrets of diviners
The nations believe in nothing
questions.explanation: The passage presents Israel’s faithfulness to the Lord as the opposite of the nations’ reliance on diviners.

questions.question: What does “which thou shalt possess” imply in the context of this command?
answers: Israel must adopt the customs of the people in the land
Even after possessing the land, Israel must not adopt its inhabitants’ practices
Israel will never enter the land
questions.explanation: The passage warns that even when Israel possesses the land, it must remain separate from the practices of its former inhabitants.

questions.question: What important contrast is expressed by “but as for thee”?
answers: It compares Israel with the nations
It says that the nations do not exist
It emphasizes a clear difference between Israel and the nations
questions.explanation: The phrase marks a strong contrast: Israel is not to follow the ways of the nations.

paragraphs.title: The Promise of a Prophet and Listening to His Words

easy.question: Who will raise up the prophet for the people?
answers: The Lord, the God of Israel
The people
A foreign king
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord their God will raise up the prophet.

easy.question: Where will the prophet come from?
answers: From another land
From among the people’s fellow Israelites
From the royal family only
easy.explanation: The prophet will come from among Israel’s own people, from among their brethren.

easy.question: Whom is the people commanded to listen to?
answers: The city elders
Anyone who is wise
The prophet
easy.explanation: The passage commands the people to listen to the prophet whom the Lord will raise up.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites ask not to hear the Lord’s voice directly again?
answers: Because they feared the voice, the fire, and death
Because they did not understand the language
Because they wanted to leave the wilderness
medium.explanation: The people feared hearing the Lord’s voice and seeing the great fire, lest they die.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence of events in these verses?
answers: The prophet spoke, the people asked for fire, and the Lord raised a prophet
The people asked not to hear directly, the Lord approved their request, and promised to raise a prophet
The Lord punished the people, and then they asked for a prophet
medium.explanation: First the people express fear of direct revelation; then the Lord says they have spoken well and promises a prophet.

medium.question: In the phrase “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren,” what does “from among” mean?
answers: From outside the people
In front of the brothers
From within the people
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the prophet will come from within Israel and will not be a stranger.

challenge.question: What is the prophet’s main role according to verse 18?
answers: To deliver the Lord’s words and commands to the people
To replace the Torah with new laws
To lead Israel’s wars
challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “I will put my words in his mouth,” and the prophet will speak everything the Lord commands.

challenge.question: What will happen to a person who does not listen to the prophet speaking in the Lord’s name?
answers: He will become a prophet
The Lord will hold him accountable
He may ignore him without consequence
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “I will require it of him,” meaning that the Lord will demand an account from anyone who does not listen.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the people’s request and the promise of a prophet?
answers: The people asked that the Lord never speak again
The prophet was meant to end the relationship between the Lord and the people
The prophet would serve as an intermediary conveying the Lord’s word to the people
challenge.explanation: Because the people feared direct revelation, the Lord promised to speak to them through a prophet from among their own people.

questions.question: What is the prophet’s main role according to verse 18?
answers: To deliver the Lord’s words and commands to the people
To replace the Torah with new laws
To lead Israel’s wars
questions.explanation: The Lord says, “I will put my words in his mouth,” and the prophet will speak everything the Lord commands.

questions.question: What will happen to a person who does not listen to the prophet speaking in the Lord’s name?
answers: He will become a prophet
The Lord will hold him accountable
He may ignore him without consequence
questions.explanation: The passage says, “I will require it of him,” meaning that the Lord will demand an account from anyone who does not listen.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the people’s request and the promise of a prophet?
answers: The people asked that the Lord never speak again
The prophet was meant to end the relationship between the Lord and the people
The prophet would serve as an intermediary conveying the Lord’s word to the people
questions.explanation: Because the people feared direct revelation, the Lord promised to speak to them through a prophet from among their own people.

paragraphs.title: Distinguishing a True Prophet from a False Prophet

easy.question: What is the punishment for a prophet who speaks in the Lord’s name without being commanded?
answers: The prophet shall die
The prophet shall receive a gift
The prophet shall move to another city
easy.explanation: Verse 20 states explicitly that the prophet shall die.

easy.question: How can one know that a message was not spoken by the Lord?
answers: If the prophet is young
If the message does not come to pass
If the people dislike the prophet
easy.explanation: Verse 22 teaches that if what is spoken in the Lord’s name does not happen, it was not spoken by the Lord.

easy.question: In whose name might a prophet also speak, according to verse 20?
answers: In the king’s name
In the people’s name
In the name of other gods
easy.explanation: The passage also warns against a prophet who speaks in the name of other gods.

medium.question: What is the purpose of the question “How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken?”
answers: To ask the prophet to speak more loudly
To explain how to test whether the prophet’s words are true
To ask where the prophet lives
medium.explanation: The question leads to the test given in the next verse: whether the prediction comes to pass.

medium.question: In the phrase “the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name,” what does “presume” mean?
answers: Forget to speak
Speak quietly
Dare to speak arrogantly and deliberately
medium.explanation: The word describes someone who speaks deliberately and presumptuously in the Lord’s name without being commanded.

medium.question: What is the conclusion when a message spoken in the Lord’s name does not come to pass?
answers: The prophet spoke presumptuously and not from the Lord
The people must wait many more years
The prophet received another prophecy
medium.explanation: Verse 22 says that if the word does not happen, the prophet spoke presumptuously.

challenge.question: Why does the verse emphasize both “if the thing follow not” and “nor come to pass”?
answers: To describe two different prophets
To teach that every prophecy happens immediately
To emphasize that the predicted thing did not happen at all
challenge.explanation: The repetition strengthens the idea that the prophecy completely failed to take place.

challenge.question: What does the command “thou shalt not be afraid of him” mean at the end of the passage?
answers: The people must not fear the false prophet
The people must not speak with the prophet
The people must not follow the prophet to another city
challenge.explanation: Once the prophet is shown to have spoken presumptuously, the people must not recognize his authority or fear him.

challenge.question: What detail is shared by the two kinds of prophets mentioned in verse 20?
answers: Both immediately repent
Both speak in a name that has not commanded them
Both announce something that will happen
challenge.explanation: The verse includes a prophet who speaks in the Lord’s name without being commanded and one who speaks in the name of other gods; both are false prophets.

questions.question: Why does the verse emphasize both “if the thing follow not” and “nor come to pass”?
answers: To describe two different prophets
To teach that every prophecy happens immediately
To emphasize that the predicted thing did not happen at all
questions.explanation: The repetition strengthens the idea that the prophecy completely failed to take place.

questions.question: What does the command “thou shalt not be afraid of him” mean at the end of the passage?
answers: The people must not fear the false prophet
The people must not speak with the prophet
The people must not follow the prophet to another city
questions.explanation: Once the prophet is shown to have spoken presumptuously, the people must not recognize his authority or fear him.

questions.question: What detail is shared by the two kinds of prophets mentioned in verse 20?
answers: Both immediately repent
Both speak in a name that has not commanded them
Both announce something that will happen
questions.explanation: The verse includes a prophet who speaks in the Lord’s name without being commanded and one who speaks in the name of other gods; both are false prophets.
